hints: At a constant speed on a level road, the driving force equals the resistance force: $F = 1400\text{ N}$.
Use $P = Fv$ with $F = 1400\text{ N}$ and $v = 28\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Calculate $1400 \times 28$ in watts and divide by $1000$ to express the power in kW.
walkthrough:
At constant speed on a horizontal road, driving force balances the resistance:
$$F = R = 1400\text{ N}$$

Calculate the power in watts and convert to kilowatts:
$$P = F \times v = 1400 \times 28 = 39\,200\text{ W} = 39.2\text{ kW}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the force balance condition for motion at constant speed on a level road:
Because the car travels at constant speed, its acceleration is zero ($a = 0$).
By Newton's first law, the forward driving force $F$ produced by the engine must equal the opposing resistance force $R$:
$$F = R = 1400\text{ N}$$

Apply the power-force-velocity relation:
$$P = F \times v$$
Substitute the values $F = 1400\text{ N}$ and $v = 28\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$P = 1400 \times 28\text{ W}$$

Convert the result to kilowatts by dividing by $1000$:
$$P = \frac{39\,200}{1000} = 39.2\text{ kW}$$
Thus, the rate at which the engine is working is $39.2\text{ kW}$ (or $39.3\text{ kW}$ to 3 significant figures).

hints: Express the driving force in terms of the power $43.5\text{ kW} = 43\,500\text{ W}$ and speed $v$: $F_D = \frac{43\,500}{v}$.
At constant speed uphill, driving force balances the sum of resistance and the downhill component of weight: $F_D = R + mg\sin\theta$.
Substitute $R = 1400\text{ N}$, $m = 1250\text{ kg}$, $g = 10$, and $\sin\theta = 0.12$ to find $F_D = 2900\text{ N}$, then solve for $v$.
walkthrough:
Resolve forces parallel to the hill at constant speed ($a = 0$):
$$F_D - R - mg\sin\theta = 0$$
$$F_D = 1400 + (1250)(10)(0.12) = 1400 + 1500 = 2900\text{ N}$$

Equate driving force to $\frac{P}{v}$ with $P = 43\,500\text{ W}$:
$$\frac{43\,500}{v} = 2900$$

Solve for the steady speed $v$:
$$v = \frac{43\,500}{2900} = \frac{435}{29} = 15\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Analyze the forces acting on the car along the inclined hill:
- Forward driving force: $F_D$
- Opposing resistance force: $R = 1400\text{ N}$
- Downhill component of weight: $W_{\parallel} = mg\sin\theta$
Substitute $m = 1250\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and $\sin\theta = 0.12$:
$$W_{\parallel} = (1250)(10)(0.12) = 12\,500 \times 0.12 = 1500\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law along the slope for steady speed ($a = 0$):
$$\sum F = 0$$
$$F_D - R - mg\sin\theta = 0$$
$$F_D = 1400 + 1500 = 2900\text{ N}$$

Relate the driving force to the engine's power output:
$$P = 43.5\text{ kW} = 43\,500\text{ W}$$
$$F_D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{43\,500}{v}$$

Equate the two expressions for driving force:
$$\frac{43\,500}{v} = 2900$$
Multiply both sides by $v$ and divide by $2900$:
$$v = \frac{43\,500}{2900} = \frac{435}{29}$$
Since $29 \times 15 = 435$:
$$v = 15\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Thus, the constant speed of the car up the hill is $15\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

hints: Treat the car and trailer as a single combined system of total mass $1250 + 600 = 1850\text{ kg}$ to find acceleration $a$.
Total downhill forces on the system: $R_{\text{car}} + R_{\text{trailer}} + (m_C + m_T)g\sin\theta = 1400 + 300 + 1850(10)(0.12) = 3920\text{ N}$.
Apply $F_{\text{net}} = ma$: $5000 - 3920 = 1850a$, then isolate the trailer $T - 300 - 600(10)(0.12) = 600a$ to find $T$.
walkthrough:
Apply Newton's second law to the whole system (car and trailer) along the inclined slope:
$$F_D - R_{\text{car}} - R_{\text{trailer}} - (m_C + m_T)g\sin\theta = (m_C + m_T)a$$
$$5000 - 1400 - 300 - (1250 + 600)(10)(0.12) = (1250 + 600)a$$
$$3300 - 1850(1.2) = 1850a$$
$$3300 - 2220 = 1850a \implies 1080 = 1850a$$

Solve for the acceleration $a$:
$$a = \frac{1080}{1850} = \frac{108}{185} \approx 0.584\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Apply Newton's second law to the trailer alone to find tension $T$ in the cable:
$$T - R_{\text{trailer}} - m_T g\sin\theta = m_T a$$
$$T - 300 - 600(10)(0.12) = 600\left(\frac{108}{185}\right)$$
$$T - 1020 = \frac{12\,960}{37} \implies T = 1020 + \frac{12\,960}{37} = \frac{50\,700}{37} \approx 1370\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Analyze the connected car-trailer system:
- Mass of car: $m_C = 1250\text{ kg}$, resistance: $R_C = 1400\text{ N}$
- Mass of trailer: $m_T = 600\text{ kg}$, resistance: $R_T = 300\text{ N}$
- Total mass of system: $M = 1250 + 600 = 1850\text{ kg}$
- Driving force produced by car: $F_D = 5000\text{ N}$
- Slope angle: $\sin\theta = 0.12$

Calculate the total opposing forces on the combined system:
- Total resistance: $R_{\text{total}} = 1400 + 300 = 1700\text{ N}$
- Total downhill component of weight: $W_{\parallel,\text{total}} = Mg\sin\theta = (1850)(10)(0.12) = 18\,500 \times 0.12 = 2220\text{ N}$
- Total resisting force: $1700 + 2220 = 3920\text{ N}$

Apply Newton's second law along the slope to the system:
$$\sum F = M a$$
$$F_D - (R_{\text{total}} + W_{\parallel,\text{total}}) = M a$$
$$5000 - 3920 = 1850a$$
$$1080 = 1850a$$
Divide by $1850$:
$$a = \frac{1080}{1850} = \frac{108}{185} \approx 0.58378\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $a = 0.584\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

Isolate the trailer to determine the tension $T$ in the connecting cable:
Forces acting on the trailer parallel to the slope:
- Forward tension pulling uphill: $T$
- Backward resistance: $R_T = 300\text{ N}$
- Backward component of weight: $m_T g\sin\theta = (600)(10)(0.12) = 720\text{ N}$
Apply Newton's second law to the trailer:
$$T - R_T - m_T g\sin\theta = m_T a$$
$$T - 300 - 720 = 600\left(\frac{108}{185}\right)$$
$$T - 1020 = \frac{600 \times 108}{185} = \frac{120 \times 108}{37} = \frac{12\,960}{37}$$
Add $1020$ to both sides:
$$T = 1020 + \frac{12\,960}{37} = \frac{1020 \times 37 + 12\,960}{37} = \frac{37\,740 + 12\,960}{37} = \frac{50\,700}{37}\text{ N}$$
Compute the decimal equivalent:
$$T = 1370.27\ldots \approx 1370\text{ N}$$
Thus, the acceleration is $0.584\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and the tension in the cable is $1370\text{ N}$.
